entities.summary:
Alfonso Enríquez, also known as Alonso Enríquez (died 1429), was a pivotal figure in late medieval Castile, serving as the first Lord of Medina de Rioseco and, most significantly, as Admiral of Castile. A natural son of Fadrique Alfonso, Master of the Order of Santiago and illegitimate son of King Alfonso XI of Castile, Alfonso Enríquez established one of the most powerful and enduring noble houses in the Iberian Peninsula, the Enríquez de Mendoza, through strategic marriages and military prowess. His career spanned the reigns of Henry III and John II, during which he played a crucial role in consolidating Castilian naval power and projecting its influence across the Atlantic and Mediterranean.

His tenure as Admiral of Castile, commencing in 1407, marked a period of significant naval activity and administrative reform. Alfonso Enríquez commanded Castilian fleets in numerous engagements, notably against Portugal during the Castilian-Portuguese Wars and in campaigns against the Nasrid Kingdom of Granada, securing Castilian dominance in regional waters. He also engaged in political maneuvering within the turbulent Castilian court, aligning with various factions to protect and expand his family's interests and influence, particularly during the minority of John II, where he was a key member of the regency council.

entities.summary:
Alfonso Enríquez (1354–1429) was the first Admiral of Castile from the Trastámara dynasty, a pivotal figure in solidifying royal power and establishing one of Spain's most enduring noble lineages. As an illegitimate son of King Henry II of Castile, Alfonso's life spanned the tumultuous consolidation of the Trastámara monarchy, during which he leveraged his royal blood and military prowess to ascend to the highest echelons of Castilian society, becoming Lord of Medina de Rioseco and progenitor of the powerful Enríquez family.

His career was defined by significant naval and political contributions to the Castilian crown. Appointed Admiral of Castile in 1405 by his half-brother, King Henry III, Alfonso Enríquez played a crucial role in defending Castilian maritime interests, particularly against the Portuguese. He commanded fleets in various engagements, notably participating in the Castilian-Portuguese Wars and contributing to the defense of the Straits of Gibraltar against Moroccan incursions. Beyond naval command, he was a key advisor during the minority of John II, navigating complex court politics and regional rivalries, thereby securing his family's position as a major force in the kingdom.

The legacy of Alfonso Enríquez is primarily etched in the establishment of the House of Enríquez, which, through strategic marriages and land acquisitions, became the Dukes of Medina de Rioseco and Counts of Melgar. His descendants included Joanna Enríquez, mother of Ferdinand II of Aragon, thereby making Alfonso the great-great-grandfather of Ferdinand and a direct ancestor of the Catholic Monarchs, Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand II of Aragon, whose union forged modern Spain. His efforts transformed the admiralty from a mere title into a powerful, dynastic office, integral to Castilian imperial ambitions.
